$schema: See shared/collectionShapes.ts for the loader and the rules each field drives.
$doc: Hand-verified shape of TMDB collections whose membership is NOT a narrative prerequisite chain.
The default assumption — every release-adjacent pair in a collection is a 'you must watch this
first' edge — is right for a tight sequel series (Harry Potter, John Wick, Dune) and wrong for
three other kinds of collection that TMDB models identically:
episodic  An anthology or an episodic franchise. Entries share a brand, not a story. Chaining
them produces the single worst output this feature can make: 'Part 24 of 27 —
everything else comes first' on a film you can watch cold.
arcs      Several independent stories in one collection object (separate trilogies, a reboot
timeline, a prequel line). Chaining across the boundary invents a prerequisite.
exclude   A spin-off, recap, or alternate cut that sits inside the collection but outside its
story. It should not occupy a link in the chain.
Deliberately a hand-verified list, not a heuristic — matching the reasoning already in
scripts/sync_relations_tmdb.py. Size is the tempting signal and it does not work: Harry Potter
has 8 parts and is a real chain, while Predator has 6 and is not. A size fallback still exists
(shared/collectionShapes.ts EPISODIC_PART_THRESHOLD) but only far above anything legitimate.
'arcs' and 'story' hold TMDB movie ids. 'arcs' groups are the continuity chains; any part not
listed in one is treated as loose and gets 'same series, not required' Can Watch edges instead.
'story' is the full narrative order for the connections view's Story-order toggle, and is only
needed where it differs from release order.
Run `python scripts/audit_collection_shapes.py` to list collections in the database that reach
the chain path without an entry here, ranked by how many titles they affect.

10.name: Star Wars Collection
10.note: Two lines, not three. The sequel trilogy continues the original directly (The Force Awakens picks up Luke, Leia and Han thirty years on), so those six are one arc; the prequels stand apart and are required by neither. This matches what data/relations_seed.json already asserts by hand: 'The Force Awakens --before--> Return of the Jedi', and no edge between the prequels and anything else. The naive walk instead emits 'Return of the Jedi before The Phantom Menace'.
10.storyNote: In-universe chronology, and deliberately wider than the collection: `story` is read as a flat tmdb id -> rank map (shared/collectionShapes.ts storyRank), so it can place the films and series that sit inside this franchise's timeline without being members of TMDB collection 10 — The Clone Wars, Rebels, Andor, Rogue One, The Mandalorian, Ahsoka. Without them the toggle pushes every unranked title to the end of the line, which put Rogue One after The Rise of Skywalker when it belongs in the minutes before A New Hope. Tales of the Jedi and Tales of the Empire are left out on purpose: an anthology spanning several eras has no single position.

645.name: James Bond Collection
645.note: 27 parts across six actors and two continuities. Only the Craig films have real continuity, and Never Say Never Again is not even an Eon film.

1745820.name: Untold Collection
1745820.note: Netflix sports-documentary anthology. Every entry is a self-contained film about a different subject.

4246.name: Scary Movie Collection
4246.note: Parody anthology, plus a 2026 reboot that reuses the first film's title.

91361.name: Halloween Collection
91361.note: Three mutually exclusive timelines, and Halloween III shares nothing with any of them.

9735.name: Friday the 13th Collection
9735.note: Episodic slasher series; entries are watchable in any order.

399.name: Predator Collection
399.note: Predators, The Predator, Prey and Badlands are each standalone.

142015.name: Housefull Collection
142015.note: Indian comedy anthology — recurring cast, unrelated stories.

483464.name: Golmaal Collection
483464.note: Indian comedy anthology — recurring cast, unrelated stories.

142021.name: Dhamaal Collection
142021.note: Indian comedy anthology — recurring cast, unrelated stories.

90863.name: Rush Hour Collection
90863.note: Standalone buddy-cop cases; no entry assumes another.

192492.name: The Jack Ryan Collection
192492.note: Recast across every film; each adapts a separate novel.

261590.name: Living Dead Collection
261590.note: Romero's films share a premise, not a cast or a plot; each stands alone.

748.name: X-Men Collection
748.note: Original trilogy and the First Class prequel line are separate continuities that Days of Future Past deliberately splits apart.

528.name: The Terminator Collection
528.note: Genisys and Dark Fate each reboot from Judgment Day and contradict the middle films, so neither continues the T1-Salvation line.

228446.name: Insidious Collection
228446.note: Chapter 3 and The Last Key are prequels; The Red Door continues Chapter 2 directly across them.

495527.name: Jumanji Collection
495527.note: The 1995 film is a separate story the Welcome to the Jungle line only nods to.

328.name: Jurassic Park Collection
328.note: The Jurassic World films restart with a new cast a generation later.

9485.name: The Fast and the Furious Collection
9485.note: Tokyo Drift is set after Fast & Furious 6 despite releasing third; Hobbs & Shaw is a side story.

230.name: The Godfather Collection
230.note: Coda is a re-edit of Part III, not a fourth film.

31562.name: The Bourne Collection
31562.note: The Bourne Legacy follows Aaron Cross and Bourne does not appear.

656.name: Saw Collection
656.note: Spiral is a standalone spin-off with none of the series' characters.

8354.name: Ice Age Collection
8354.note: The Adventures of Buck Wild is a spin-off with a different lead.

383987.name: Attack on Titan Collection
383987.note: Chronicle is a recap compilation of the earlier films, not a new chapter.
